frase: Hello, everyone! Colonel Roosevelt here. It is three o'clock in the morning, I am in a hospital bed in Chicago... and there is a bullet in my chest. I feel bully! Let me tell you how my Monday went.
vozes: A 54-year-old American man from New York in 1912, upper-class old New York accent. Surprisingly high-pitched, reedy tenor voice, very energetic and emphatic, crisp clipped consonants, bursts of enthusiasm, speaks fast then punches key words, cheerful and slightly hoarse.

A vigorous American politician in his fifties with an old-fashioned East Coast patrician accent. Bright, nasal, high tenor voice, explosive delivery, big grin audible in the voice, short staccato phrases, booming exclamations like a stump speaker.

A barrel-chested 54-year-old American colonel speaking with an early 1900s New York accent. Thin, high, slightly squeaky voice that contrasts with his big presence, extremely enthusiastic and comedic, rapid confident pace, chuckling between sentences.

An energetic older American gentleman from 1912 Manhattan, refined Knickerbocker accent. Clear high-pitched voice with a raspy edge from too many speeches, joyful, theatrical, emphatic stress on every important word, like a charismatic showman telling a wild story.
